body:
# EngineShelf 1.1.7

## Fixed

- **The Windows manager would not start on a machine without WSL 2.** `wsl -l -q`
  answers on stderr there, Windows PowerShell turns that into an error record, and
  `$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'` made it terminate the script — from the startup
  container scan, before the first request. So `EngineShelf.bat` printed
  Microsoft's "not installed" line and stopped, on machines that only ever wanted
  the native launcher. The `2>$null` on that line never suppressed it: the record
  is raised first and redirected after. Every `wsl` call sits behind a helper that
  lowers the preference for exactly the length of the call now.
- **The WSL 2 row in the system check promised the wrong thing.** With the feature
  switched off it read as "WSL is enabled and has no Linux in it yet … nothing to
  answer", which hid both the administrator prompt and the restart. One command
  covers both states it can be in, and the note says both.
- **What the manager asks the machine at startup can no longer take it down.**
  `server.py` asks it on a daemon thread, where a throw costs the answer;
  `gui/server.ps1` is one thread serving HTTP and had nowhere for it to land.

Windows only. macOS and Linux are unchanged from 1.1.6.

## Upgrading

- **Take this if you are on Windows.** Without WSL 2 installed, 1.1.6 does not open
  the manager at all.
- Nothing else to do: extract over the old copy and start it. Browsers, profiles
  and containers are untouched.

Artifacts: `EngineShelf-1.1.7-macOS.zip`, `EngineShelf-1.1.7-Windows.zip`,
`EngineShelf-1.1.7-Linux.tar.gz`. Verify with `SHA256SUMS.txt`.
